parts.note: a mouse is a timid person, so a feline one is a cat with no courage, which is a playground name for a coward

explanation.surface: A puzzling creature that is half cat, half rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' looks like the animal, but here it means a timid person; a feline timid person is a frightened cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish insult for a coward, literally a cat that is frightened, which fits a mousy cat.

clue.text: Explosive — terribly angered or extraordinarily enraged!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the following word are badly disordered and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone so furious they are ready to go off like a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives two routes: 'terribly' rearranges ANGERED and 'extraordinarily' rearranges ENRAGED; both sets of letters are the same, so either gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is an explosive device, so the noun sense of explosive fits.

clue.text: Native of a sultanate — returning shortly

indicators.note: returning means the phrase for shortly is read backwards

parts.note: shortly means in a moment, abbreviated to 'in a mo'

explanation.surface: A local from a Gulf state will be back soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' is the informal 'in a mo', and 'returning' turns INAMO round.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is ruled by a sultan, so a person born there is a native of a sultanate.

parts.note: so can mean very, as in 'so good'
so again stands for very

explanation.surface: Something emphatically mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or merely passable, the sense of an average performance.

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is a slang word for cannabis

explanation.surface: Mixing two narcotics is a ridiculous idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy or absurd scheme is described with this adjective, a synonym for eccentric and foolish.

definitions.meaning: used as an adverb meaning truly or in fact
said as a question expressing doubt or surprise, like 'is that so?'

explanation.surface: Someone affirming a point, then doubting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an emphatic adverb meaning truly and as an incredulous question.

indicators.note: confiscating means the word for also takes the luggage inside itself

parts.note: too means also
a bag is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: Customs on an island seize travellers' cases as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island, paired with Trinidad as one nation.

clue.text: A selection from menu, that choice bird

indicators.note: selection from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Picking a dish off the menu that is a good choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird that cracks nuts, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Ashgabat, Singapore, Islamabad? All capitals here

definitions.text: Ashgabat, Singapore, Islamabad? All capitals here

indicators.note: capitals means the capital letters, the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: Three capital cities, all found on the same continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' works twice: these are capital cities, and their capital letters plus that of 'All' spell the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkmenistan, Singapore and Pakistan lie on this continent, so their capitals are found there.

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of the next word are muddled into nonsense

explanation.surface: Calling bright people idiotic names.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony: 'Stupid' is the anagram signal for a society of the clever.
explanation.definitionFit: The society for people with very high IQ scores, so a body of clever people.

clue.text: Bloody Mary cocktail for Russian fighters

parts.note: bloody means red, the colour of blood

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the name are mixed

explanation.surface: Soldiers from Moscow ordering a vodka-and-tomato drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody Mary' reads as the name of the drink, but the two words must be split, with 'cocktail' as the mixing signal rather than part of the bar order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet army was known by this name, so its soldiers were Russian fighters.

clue.text: Enter time for recollection after end of career — this?

definitions.text: Enter time for recollection after end of career — this?

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word
re-collection means gathering the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: After a working life ends, there is time to reminisce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollection' looks like memory but is read as re-collection, rearranging ENTER, TIME and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping work for good at the close of a career, when there is time to look back.

indicators.note: adopting means the shortened word takes the other inside it
almost means the last letter of the word for man is dropped

parts.note: a chap is a man
else means different, as in 'someone else'

explanation.surface: A man nearly signing for a rival club.
explanation.definitionFit: A London football club, so an example of a team.

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning bring up, as children
a noun meaning backside or back part

explanation.surface: Lift your backside.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to bring up; as a noun it means the backside.

clue.text: Pedestrian ready to wander round river

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
to wander suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker prepared to roam around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To wander' rearranges READY into DEARY, which goes round R. 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker but is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and uninspired, a synonym for tedious.

parts.note: an express is a fast train, and small children call a train by the sound its engine makes

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something into baby talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb meaning to say, but it is the noun, a fast train.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery word for a railway engine, imitating the puffing of steam.

clue.text: Vehicle — parking one on the street

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Leaving a vehicle parked by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeless vagrant lives on the streets, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: Sorting letters, indicatory as reference book

indicators.note: sorting the letters means putting them into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging words alphabetically, as a reference book does.
explanation.definitionFit: A book listing words with meanings, consulted for reference.

clue.text: Love of food beginning to grow, following the stars?

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the next word

parts.note: following the stars describes the study of the heavens

explanation.surface: A growing appetite, perhaps guided by astrology.
explanation.definitionFit: The art and appreciation of fine eating, which is a love of good cooking.

clue.text: Fair trial's conclusion welcomed by philistine

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken inside the word for philistine

parts.note: a peasant is an uncultured person, a philistine

indicators.note: conclusion picks the final letter of the word trial

explanation.surface: A boor approving the end of a just hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is nice and agreeable, a synonym sense of the adjective.

parts.note: also means too
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A loser who was also rushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or runner who finished outside the places, so a loser in a race.

parts.note: a score is twenty
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer making twenty runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who puts the ball in the net makes goals, a goal-getter.

indicators.note: sounding means the word for the banknote is said out loud

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A musical note sounded for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical but is a banknote: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice in the high range, and the man who sings it.

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word for manufactured is written backwards

parts.note: made means manufactured

explanation.surface: Cheese that was produced badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A round Dutch cheese with red wax, an example of a cheese.
